name: Metabase
description: Open source business intelligence and analytics platform. Create dashboards and explore data without writing SQL.
summary: Metabase is actively maintained with frequent patch releases across multiple supported version branches. The latest release is v0.63.2 (open source) / v1.63.2 (enterprise), released on July 29, 2025. Multiple version lines (58.x, 59.x, 60.x, 61.x, 62.x, 63.x) are receiving concurrent patch updates, indicating a mature, actively supported project. Detailed changelogs are linked per release at https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Open Source edition uses AGPL v3; Enterprise edition uses a commercial license. See https://www.metabase.com/license/
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple patch releases across 6 version branches were published on July 28–29, 2025.
answers.Is there a cloud-hosted version availabl: Yes — Metabase Cloud is available at https://www.metabase.com (managed cloud offering).
answers.Does it support SSO and SAML authenticat: Yes — SSO and SAML are supported in the Enterprise edition.
answers.What databases/data sources are supporte: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite, BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, Athena, Spark SQL, MongoDB, Presto, Druid, Oracle, Vertica, and more via drivers.

alternatives.name: Redash
alternatives.review: Open source, query-focused, simpler feature set.

alternatives.name: Apache Superset
alternatives.review: Apache-licensed, rich visualisation library, steeper setup curve.

alternatives.name: Grafana
alternatives.review: Primarily metrics/time-series but increasingly used for general BI.

alternatives.name: Hex
alternatives.review: Close source, enterprise focus, AI Analytics Platform for your whole team

alternatives.name: Tableau
alternatives.review: Offers far more advanced visualization and analytics capabilities than Metabase but is proprietary, expensive, and not self-hostable in the open-source sense.

alternatives.name: Lightdash
alternatives.review: Tightly integrates with dbt for a metrics-layer-first approach, making it more suitable for dbt-heavy teams but less general-purpose than Metabase.
